lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: personal safety and check-in plans

objective: The learner and a trusted adult set up and agree on one real check-in protocol for a real time the learner will be away from home (for example, walking to a friend's house, biking to a store, or attending an activity), specifying exactly how and when the learner will check in.
scenario: The learner identifies one real upcoming time they will be away from home without a trusted adult directly present, proposes a specific check-in plan (such as a message on arrival, a check-in at an agreed time, or checking in at each waypoint of a route), and the trusted adult reviews, adjusts if needed, and agrees to the plan before the outing.
safetyNotes: The learner does not need to be away from home during the lesson itself; only setting up and agreeing on the plan with a trusted adult is required.
This task never requires the learner to travel anywhere alone as part of completing the lesson; if there is no real upcoming time away from home, the fictional-scenario alternative is used instead.
Completing this task sheet never certifies the agreement by itself; a guardian confirmation is required before the task counts as complete.

simulationAlternative.description: If there is no real upcoming time the learner will be away from home, the learner instead designs a full check-in plan for a realistic fictional outing (such as walking to a friend's house across town or attending an evening activity) and presents the complete plan to a trusted adult for the same level of review and agreement, including the adult's feedback on what they would change.

materials: paper or a document to write the check-in plan
a phone or other communication method the household already uses, if applicable

tasks.directions: Think about a real upcoming time you'll be away from home, or a realistic fictional outing if you don't have one.

prompts.text: Describe the outing: where you're going, how you're getting there, and roughly how long you'll be gone.

tasks.directions: Draft a specific check-in plan naming exactly when and how you will check in.

prompts.text: My plan names a specific method of checking in (such as a text message, a phone call, or checking in in person at a specific point).
My plan names a specific time or trigger for each check-in (such as 'on arrival' or 'by 6:00 pm').
My plan includes what happens if I miss a check-in (who gets contacted and what they do next).

tasks.directions: Present your plan to a trusted adult and agree on a final version together.

prompts.text: Did your trusted adult agree to your plan as written, or did they ask for a change?
choices: They agreed to it as written

prompts.text: Write the final, agreed-on version of your check-in plan, including any change your trusted adult asked for.

tasks.directions: Think about why check-in plans matter.

prompts.text: Explain what could go wrong if you left for this outing without an agreed check-in plan, and how the plan you made would help.

remediation: If a learner's plan is missing a specific trigger (such as writing 'I'll check in sometime') or a missed-check-in step, reteach by having them rewrite the plan using exact times and a named first contact, comparing a vague version side-by-side with a specific version before finalizing the plan with their adult.
extension: Have the learner design a second check-in plan for a longer or higher-stakes outing (such as an overnight activity) and explain what changes about the plan when the stakes are higher.
